Here's the complete roadmap to master AI tools from beginner to AI researcher.

---

1. Level 0 starts with AI awareness through prompting, questions, summaries, and content generation.

---

2. Learn core AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot first.

---

3. Level 1 focuses on becoming an AI power user for daily productivity and research.

---

4. Master advanced prompting, brainstorming, document analysis, and writing workflows.

---

5. Use AI for research, meetings, notes, and professional writing every day.

---

6. Level 2 teaches multimodal creation with text, images, videos, voice, and presentations.

---

7. Learn image generation, video creation, presentation design, and social media workflows.

---

8. Explore tools like MidJourney, Ideogram, Runway, Pika, Canva, Gamma, and HeyGen.

---

9. Level 3 is about automating repetitive work with AI workflows.

---

10. Build automations for CRM, content pipelines, triggers, and APIs using no code tools.

---

11. Level 4 teaches you how to build powerful AI agents with memory, RAG, and tool calling.

---

12. Learn frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Flowise, and LangFlow.

---

13. Level 5 focuses on AI coding, debugging, testing, and building full stack applications.

---

14. Use coding tools like Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Windsurf, and Replit Agent.

---

15. Level 6 expands into building AI powered businesses with marketing, sales, and analytics.

---

16. Level 7 covers designing complete AI systems with orchestration, governance, and security.

---

17. Learn model routing, observability, evaluation, and human in the loop systems.

---

18. Level 8 pushes into AI research with fine tuning, benchmarking, multimodal research, and safety.

---

19. Follow the roadmap month by month to steadily progress from beginner to expert.

---

20. AI mastery in 2026 is increasingly about agents, automation, multimodal creation, and AI powered systems.

Let's be real here. As an Italian who has been working with CNNs, Diffusion Architecture, RL, and machine learning projects since 2021, it is frankly baffling that in 2026, a model like Emma fails to outperform even the original GPT-2 architecture.

Developing a highly capable LLM based on modern architectures (like Qwen) is more accessible than ever. With the right data and a small budget, taking a strong base model through pre-training progression and post-training fixes to achieve near-frontier performance is a standard practice today.

Emma isn't just a bad product resulting from a lack of technical competence; it is being aggressively overhyped. Presenting an underwhelming, underperforming, and expensive model does not prove that "Italy is joining the ML game." Instead, it highlights our systemic inability to properly innovate and build robust new technologies.

This exact culture is why I left Italy to work elsewhere in Europe. Working in the Italian tech ecosystem often slows you down, especially when the community insists on praising flawed products rather than demanding excellence or pivoting to riskier, cutting-edge approaches (like the sparse attention architectures we're seeing from the new Chinese models).

We need to stop applauding mediocrity if we ever want to actually compete.

If you want to work faster, create better content, and get more done with less effort, these tools are worth exploring:

1. 🤖 ChatGPT — Write, brainstorm, code, and solve problems.
2. 🖼️ PicWish — Instantly remove and edit image backgrounds.
3. 🔍 Perplexity — Get AI-powered answers with source-backed research.
4. 🎵 Suno — Create original music from simple prompts.

6. 🎙️ ElevenLabs — Generate incredibly realistic AI voices.

10. 🎬 Runway — Edit and generate videos with AI.

12. 🎥 Syllaby — Create faceless videos for social media.

⚡ These tools can help you save time, increase productivity, and create higher-quality content without spending hours on repetitive tasks.
